findings.F1: The move per case is too small to pay for a trade, and the coin's own rise works against the short: over the 48 hours after the 717 active weekends the short's total move is −0.18 % (t −0.75), and the step-5 size is +0.03 % total and +0.29 % unusual, against a 0.19 % cost per trade.
findings.F2: The book pays the cost about twice per weekend and loses on most trades: 1,796 short trades on about 952 active weekends (459 lasted under 1.5 h and 348 lasted 1.5–24 h), a mean of 42.6 allocation changes inside each 48-hour hold, a gross mean of −0.93 % and a net mean of −1.03 % per trade, and 26 % winners.
findings.F3: What happened on the weekdays before decides the sign, and the effect is larger over four days than over two: after a weekend rise that followed a weekday rise, the coin kept rising (the short's total is −0.65 % over 48 h, t −1.97, and −1.00 % over 96 h, t −2.20, 593 cases); after a weekend rise that followed a weekday fall, the short gained +0.11 % over 48 h (t 0.43) and +0.47 % over 96 h (t 1.24, 616 cases).
findings.F4: The continuation after a weekday rise is strongest when the weekend traded heavily: weekend rises after a weekday rise on volume at or above the weekday mean were followed by a further rise against the short of 1.68 % over 48 h (t −2.04, 168 cases), against +0.03 % (t 0.11, 434 cases) on thin weekends.
findings.F5: The result changes sign from year to year: the short's total over 48 h on active weekends was +0.20 % to +0.35 % in 2018–2020 and +0.86 % in 2025, but −1.56 % in 2021 (t −1.83) and −0.84 % in 2023 (t −1.79); the book's mean daily return was negative in every year from 2020 to 2024 while the coins' mean daily return was positive.
findings.F6: Weekend moves are not reversed more than weekday moves, and small and mid-sized weekend moves continue: the reversal of the 48-hour move ending at 23:00 is −0.29 % for Sunday (t −1.87) and −0.07 % to −0.24 % on weekdays; the Sunday terciles by size are −0.45 % (t −1.99), −0.58 % (t −2.32) and +0.16 % (t 0.49) for the largest.
findings.F7: The coin's 30-day return bends the result: active cases in the two outer quartiles of 30-day return gave the short +0.44 % and +0.42 %, while the two middle quartiles gave −0.85 % (t −2.08) and −0.75 % (t −1.69).

ideas.idea: A coin's Saturday-Sunday rise that follows a rise over the preceding five weekdays continues over the next four days; the larger the weekend rise and the heavier the weekend's volume against the weekdays' mean, the larger the further rise.
ideas.consequence: After a heavy-volume weekend rise that extends a rising week, a trader holds the coin long through Thursday instead of shorting it, and refuses the short that the reversal idea would take.
ideas.name: weekend rise extends rising week

ideas.idea: A coin's Saturday-Sunday rise is partly reversed over the next four days, only while its preceding five weekdays fell and its weekend volume is lower than its mean volume over those weekdays; the larger the weekend rise and the lower the weekend volume against the weekdays, the larger the share reversed.
ideas.consequence: A trader shorts a thin weekend rise only when it is a bounce inside a falling week, holds the short through Thursday, and refuses it after a rising week.
ideas.name: thin bounce in falling week

ideas.idea: A coin's Saturday-Sunday move continues in its own direction over the next 48 hours (Monday and Tuesday); the larger the move relative to the coin's usual 48-hour move, up to a usual move, the larger the continuation.
ideas.consequence: After a modest weekend move, a trader takes the side of the weekend move into Tuesday rather than fading it.
ideas.name: modest weekend moves continue
